title: Neutrino mass ordering: normal or inverted hierarchy
bottleneck: Oscillation data fix two mass-squared splittings but not their sign relative to the third state, leaving two possible orderings: normal, with the lightest state mostly electron-flavored, or inverted. Current global fits mildly favor normal ordering but cannot exclude inverted at high confidence.
why_it_blocks: The ordering determines the expected rate of neutrinoless double-beta decay, the pattern of flavor symmetry models, and whether the lightest neutrino could be nearly massless, shaping the entire theoretical landscape.
current_state: The JUNO reactor experiment and the long-baseline DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande programs are designed to resolve the ordering within the coming decade through precision matter-effect measurements. JUNO's medium-baseline reactor measurement should determine the ordering independently of matter effects, complementing the long-baseline accelerator programs, within this decade.
